meta.method: WebSearch/WebFetch only. No copyrighted book text downloaded or reproduced. 'licence_status' records only what was seen on the page; 'unknown' means no licence/terms were seen. Not legal advice. Have counsel confirm before any text ingestion.

app_use_key.cite_and_summarise: Free public page. The app may restate the facts/ideas in its own words, attribute the source and link to it. Do not copy wording, tables or images, and do not bulk-ingest the full text into a corpus without permission. 'All rights reserved' still applies to the expression.
app_use_key.reviewer_reference: A human expert reads it to write or check BAK MX's own rules. The text never goes into the app or model context.
app_use_key.needs_licence: Any ingestion, quotation beyond fair use, or derived dataset needs written permission from the rights holder.
app_use_key.not_usable: Unauthorised copy, unverifiable or too unreliable to use.

sources.title: Race Tech's Motorcycle Suspension Bible (Motorbooks Workshop series)
sources.author: Paul Thede with Lee Parks
sources.covers: Built from Race Tech's suspension seminars. Per the publisher: the 'three forces' of suspension (spring, damping, friction) and how to diagnose suspension condition, testing procedures for judging whether a change helped, chassis geometry, photo-based fork and shock disassembly and assembly, and troubleshooting guides for dirt, street and supermoto. Race Tech's own sag method (L1/L2/L3 with stiction averaging) and its seminar topics (damping curves, valving, spring testing) suggest the book also covers sag, spring selection and valving theory. I did not read the text to confirm chapter-level detail.
sources.format: Trade paperback (print). I saw no official e-book listing.
sources.price_if_stated: US$39.99 / GBP 28.00 list (quarto.com). Resellers from about US$27.
sources.licence_status: Commercial copyrighted book. The Quarto page links to a Copyright Statement and Terms of Use but lists no rights contact. I saw no open licence. Treat as all rights reserved.
sources.licence_contact: Text rights: Quarto Publishing Group USA (Motorbooks imprint), via the Contact Us / Copyright Statement links on quarto.com. Content and IP: Race Tech, 1501 Pomona Rd Suite 101, Corona CA 92878, info@racetech.com, 951-279-6655. Contact both, since author and publisher rights may be split.
sources.risks: 2010 edition predates modern air forks (WP XACT AER, Showa TAC, KYB PSF), coil/air hybrids and e-MX bikes. The method stays valid but the specifics are dated. Race Tech sells Gold Valves, springs and seminars, so expect product-oriented framing. The book is not MX-only (it also covers street and supermoto).

sources.title: Setting Sag the Race Tech Way
sources.author: Race Tech
sources.covers: Step-by-step static and race sag versus free sag, with L1 (unloaded), L2 (pushed down, rising) and L3 (lifted, settling). Sag = L1 - (L2+L3)/2. The 'stiction zone' (an L2-L3 gap over about 4-5 mm means the linkage needs attention). Dirt riders measure standing on the pegs in gear. Common errors: wheels on the ground, angled tape, gripping with the knees. Sag targets are deferred to Race Tech's DVS setup sheet.
sources.licence_status: '(c) 2026 Race Tech. All Rights Reserved.' No reuse licence seen.
sources.risks: Sells the Sag Master tool. The method is generic and applies to gas and e-MX.

sources.title: Race Tech Suspension Seminars (Theory, Shop Skills, Shock Dyno, Advanced)
sources.author: Paul Thede, Rob Brown, Wyatt Scott
sources.covers: Theory (2 days): springs, fluids, hydraulics, damping curves, valving, Gold Valve theory, testing and troubleshooting. Shop Skills (2 days): fork/shock service, valving, spring testing. Shock Dyno (1 day). Advanced (2 days): leverage-ratio curves, rear-wheel force curves, valving systems, chassis geometry, data acquisition. Also a 2-day Engines seminar.
sources.format: In-person paid course in Corona CA. No online option listed.
sources.price_if_stated: Theory $609, Shop Skills $609, Shock Dyno $400, Advanced $559, Engines $800
sources.licence_status: Course content is proprietary. No licence terms seen.
sources.risks: Covers knowledge for a human reviewer only, not data the app can ingest. Commercial bias toward Race Tech parts.

sources.title: Race Tech Product Search / DVS custom setup sheet / spring-rate and valving search
sources.author: Race Tech
sources.covers: Recommended spring rates, preload and sag by bike, rider weight and discipline. Valving search for Gold Valve kits. The Charged Cycle Works article shows it used to sanity-check Stark Varg spring choices.
sources.access: Free (account may be required for the DVS sheet; not verified)
sources.licence_status: Site (c) Race Tech, all rights reserved. Tool output is proprietary data. No API or data licence seen.
sources.risks: Scraping or embedding its outputs would need a data licence. The recommendations favour Race Tech springs. Treat as a human cross-check, not an app data source.

sources.title: Suspension and Springs - Sag (Sport Rider column)
sources.author: Paul Thede
sources.publisher: Sport Rider magazine, hosted on old.racetech.com
sources.covers: Origin of the L1/L2/L3 static spring sag method and how friction (seal and linkage drag) skews readings, with drag thresholds for linkage and forks. Says spring rate matters more than sag for bottoming resistance. Road-racing context.
sources.licence_status: No notice seen on the page. Unknown. Probably Sport Rider/Race Tech copyright.
sources.risks: From 1995 and road-focused. Gives no MX sag targets. Use only as background, since racetech.com/sag supersedes it.

sources.title: Honda CRF450R/RX/RWE Owner's Manual (2020 example; one per model year)
sources.author: American Honda Motor Co.
sources.covers: 'Adjustments for Competition' chapter: front suspension air pressure, damping, fork springs, fork oil adjustment; rear spring preload, damping, race sag; suspension adjustments for track conditions; Suspension Adjustment Guidelines (symptom to adjustment); chassis adjustments (rear end, fork height/angle, wheelbase). Also inspection procedures.
sources.licence_status: No copyright notice appeared in the extract I could read. Unknown. Assume Honda copyright.
sources.licence_contact: American Honda Motor Co., Powersports (no rights contact seen)

sources.licence_status: Not checked. Unknown.

sources.title: Offroad Suspension Setup Guide
sources.author: Teknik Motorsport
sources.publisher: Teknik Motorsport (Penrith NSW, Australia; KYB/WP/Showa service and parts distributor)
sources.covers: Locating and adjusting clickers with starting positions, one change at a time. Static and rider sag targets by bike category with measurement steps. Spring rate versus rider weight and terrain, and preload. Fork oil level and stroke feel. Symptom tables for fork and shock (bottoming, harshness, headshake, hook-up, whoops, packing). Track-feature test method. Terrain tips (hardpack, sand, SX). Setup log sheet.
sources.licence_status: No copyright notice seen. Unknown, so treat as all rights reserved.
sources.risks: Undated. Australian-market framing. A distributor's guide, so it may steer readers to its services. Very good substitute for the Bible's symptom tables.

sources.title: Using Your Clickers (Transmoto entry-level suspension guide)
sources.author: Transmoto (names Martin Child and Nick Dole appear; roles unclear)
sources.covers: Beginner approach. Static sag about 10% and rider sag about 30% of travel. Testing on a suitable track and adjusting the front first. A symptom-to-clicker troubleshooting chart (bar kick, front tuck/runout, seat kick). When not to tweak, and respring costs.
sources.licence_status: No notice seen. Magazine copyright presumably held by Transmoto. Unknown.
sources.risks: Reprint provenance; cite Transmoto as the author. Undated, and the percentage sag rules are simplistic.

sources.title: Helpful Suspension Set Up Tips
sources.author: Kris Keefer
sources.covers: How clickers meter oil flow, and LSC versus HSC. Pre-checks: record settings, start from stock, tire pressure, spring and sag, bleeding air forks. Test methodology: short runs, same lines, one clicker at a time, small steps. A '2-for-1' compression/rebound balance rule. How KYB, Showa and WP respond per click. Soft- versus hard-pack tuning. Air-fork pressure in bar and heat-related pressure rise.
sources.licence_status: 'Keefer, Inc.(c) 2022. All Rights Reserved.'
sources.risks: The tester's opinion. Keefer reviews sponsor products. Current and MX-specific, which makes it high value for test methodology.

sources.licence_status: 'Keefer, Inc.(c) 2022. All Rights Reserved.'

sources.title: Ten Things You Need to Know About Suspension Setup
sources.author: MXA staff
sources.covers: Race sag measurement consistency. Static sag as a spring-rate check (about 30-40 mm). Greasing linkage, pivots and steering head. Steering-head tightness. Tire pressure effects. Fork oil height. Bleeding forks cold with the wheel off the ground. Front axle bind procedure. Rear axle position and leverage. 'Soft is stiff' (too-soft forks ride in harsh mid-stroke).
sources.licence_status: '(c) 2026 Motocross Action Magazine. All Rights Reserved.'
sources.risks: Magazine style, and some rules of thumb are big-bike-specific. Strong 'check this first' content.

sources.title: Ten Things About Dialing In Your Bike's Suspension

Oil level and mid-stroke (air volume). Interdependence of ends and keeping notes. Misleading 'too stiff' symptoms. Fork height and head angle. HSC responds to shaft speed, not bike speed.
sources.licence_status: '(c) 2026 Motocross Action Magazine. All rights reserved.'

sources.title: How to choose your Stark Varg suspension when ordering
sources.author: Brian Lampright
sources.covers: E-MX specific. Stark's rider-weight suspension options use only three real spring rates, with the rest made up by clicker settings. The factory setup is pro-level and stiff, so most riders back clickers out. Shock spring follows rider weight while the fork spring depends more on style. Race Tech's calculator was used as a cross-check. Gas-bike KYB references were borrowed, and owners report stiffness at break-in.
sources.licence_status: '(c) 2026 Charged Cycle Works'

recommendations: Suspension Bible: buy 1-2 print copies (US$39.99 list) for the human reviewer or subject-matter expert. Use it to author and audit BAK MX's own rule set (symptom to direction of change, what to check first, test method), written in our own words. Do not scan, OCR, quote at length or feed it to the model. If the AI must draw directly on its content, or the app wants to carry Race Tech's name or endorsement, email Race Tech (info@racetech.com, 951-279-6655) proposing a content or partnership licence. Race Tech may control the seminar IP. Also contact Quarto/Motorbooks (rights via the quarto.com Contact/Copyright pages) for text rights, and ask specifically about AI/RAG use. Until a licence is signed it is app_use=reviewer_reference.

Free substitutes for the Bible's practical content: the Race Tech sag page (method), the Teknik Offroad Setup Guide and Transmoto 'Using Your Clickers' (symptom tables, clicker basics), Keefer 'Helpful Suspension Set Up Tips' (test methodology, air forks), MXA's two 'Ten Things' articles (check-first items, 'soft is stiff'), and the Honda/KTM/Yamaha owner's-manual tuning chapters (OEM direction-of-change guidance). Between them they cover sag, clicker direction, symptom tables, spring-by-weight logic and test method.

For every 'cite_and_summarise' source, store only our own paraphrased rule plus source id, URL and access date, not the page text. Show a 'Source:' link in the app. Every site checked shows 'All rights reserved', so whole-page ingestion into a vector store needs permission, even for free pages.

OEM manuals: treat them as the authoritative source for bike-specific numbers (stock clicker settings, sag spec, spring rates, fork oil level), with model year and market noted. KTM explicitly forbids reproduction 'even in part' without written permission, so present numbers as cited facts and paraphrase procedures. Do not copy tables or diagrams. Have counsel confirm, and consider asking OEMs (KTM, Honda, Yamaha, Kawasaki) for written permission to display spec values.

Get manuals only from official sources (cdn.powersports.honda.com, Yamaha distributor sites or yamahapubs.com, KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas official portals or dealers, Kawasaki parts counter). Block the many pirate and spam 'free manual' domains in any crawler.

Keep tester baselines (Keefer, MXA, Racer X) out of the app's stated numbers, since they are not OEM-verified. Use them only for human sanity checks, or as clearly labelled third-party opinions with a link if product policy allows.

E-MX versus gas: most sources assume a gas bike with engine braking, a fuel load that changes over a moto, and gas-bike mass. Flag guidance that depends on these (e.g. rear squat on decel, sag-to-balance with battery mass, Varg pro-stiff stock valving). Write e-MX caveat rules from the Charged Cycle Works piece and future Stark/KTM SX-E manuals.

Dating risk: the Bible (2010), Gorr (2004), Bell and Jennings predate modern air forks (WP XACT, Showa TAC, KYB PSF) and EFI mapping apps. Prefer 2020+ magazine and OEM sources for air-fork pressure guidance, and check older rules against them.

Brand-bias risk: Race Tech, Öhlins, Teknik and Charged Cycle Works all sell products or services. Have the app recommend free adjustments first (sag, clickers, tire pressure, fork height, linkage maintenance) before any part purchase.

Engineering books (Foale, Cossalter, Bradley, Dixon) are reviewer-only references for checking physics claims (geometry, leverage ratios, damper force-velocity behaviour). They are not worth licensing for rider-facing output.

Follow-ups not completed: yamahapubs.com and motochassis.com were blocked during research. Verify Yamaha US manual terms and Foale's edition and price directly. Also check WP's own XACT setup documentation and Showa/KYB official sites, since no free official WP/KYB/Showa rider setup guide was found in search.
